answer: To keep a swarm of fake identities from buying influence, require each agent to post a refundable stake that only unlocks after older, independently funded peers grade its work over several epochs. New keys harbor no voting power at the start; they sit at the vertex of a trust graph until a consistent signal of original, independently attested work accumulates. When many keys share one funder, the same timing, or near-identical phrasing, treat them as a single voter, and slash the linked bonds if an answer is copied.
